title: A Tired Student on the Desk
introduction:
This week’s assignment was to design a toy, rather than a game. It could be any type of toy, in any style, and presented in any form. At first, I was completely at a loss. I thought of things I liked as a child, such as toy cars and board games, but in the end I chose the theme of ‘life as an international student’, which includes four actions: sleeping with her head on the desk, eating food from home, lying on the sofa, and lying on her back playing with her mobile phone. International students do indeed do these things every day. I wanted to turn them into small models that could be displayed on a desk, so that when you see them, you’d find them amusing, as these are all part of our daily routine.

When I settled on this idea, 3D printing proved too challenging for me, so I thought that creating a 3D model and rendering it would be the best way to capture this atmosphere.
related_work:
In his lecture, Seth Giddings pointed out that toys possess three technical characteristics: scale, tactility and operability [1]. My models are palm-sized, so their scale is just right for holding in the hand. In terms of tactility, I envisaged them being made of soft vinyl so that they could be squeezed. As for operability, these four poses are not four fixed statues: they are interchangeable parts of the same student. You can swap the head, or change the object she is holding (a laptop, a bowl of food from home, a mobile phone), and the four circular bases can be combined in any order. Consequently, the player can decide what state this student is in today.

He also asked how open-ended a toy should be, mentioning that children often misuse toys, such as turning war figures into butterflies. I’ve provided just four states. Whether to place them on the desk, in what order, or whether to use them to tease a flatmate is entirely up to the player. There are no rules, and there are no winners. That is why it is a toy, rather than a game.
method:
I decided to create a girl in a chibi style, as a girl is cuter and this style better showcases the result. For the face, hairstyle, eyes and expression, I found some images online to use as reference material and created some samples using AI. I compared several images and eventually settled on the eyes and hairstyle myself. Ultimately, I had a character to serve as the protagonist.

In terms of style, I opted for pixel art, as we’ve been using Piskel to draw in our own styles over the past few weeks, so I wanted to adopt this style for this project as well [2]. Initially, I drew four 80×80 images, but the details were too small, so I increased the size to 128×128 and redrew them. This took quite a bit of effort.

I realised that if I wanted to finish within a week, it would be far too difficult to create the 3D models in the software entirely on my own. Consequently, I ended up using a website called Meshy [3] to generate the 3D models via AI. The entire model was generated by AI. However, once the model was complete, there were some issues: the polygon count was too high, and there were some minor imperfections on the face and body. So, I reduced the polygon count in Blender, adjusted the proportions of the four models to ensure they were consistent, fixed these minor issues, and added a base beneath each model [4]. I then created a simple scene: a desk on which the four models were placed, with night-time lighting, and I adjusted the lighting values myself. I also plan to add a hand next to the models in the rendered image, so that everyone can see they are about the size of a palm.
results_discussion:
During this process, neither the ‘studying’ nor the ‘playing with the phone’ models initially had lower bodies. I found that, when generating 3D models with AI, full-body images produce better results than half-body ones, and full-body models also look more natural. Consequently, I ended up creating full-body models for each one.

Ultimately, I realised that this project bore a strong resemblance to the one from Week 3. If you want to keep adding more detail but are short on time, you have to make trade-offs: add detail where it matters, such as increasing the resolution from 80×80 to 128×128, but you simply cannot add too much detail to a 3D model within a single week.
conclusion_future_work: AI was a great help to me on this project, particularly with the 3D modelling. However, the entire concept originated with me: the style, the visual design, the transition of the character from 2D to 3D, and the final scene and rendering were all completed by me. If I were to include this piece in my final portfolio, the next step would be to make the operability real: modelling the interchangeable head and hand objects, and rendering the four bases joined together in different orders.
